children: The Reserve Bank of India may have more room to tighten its policy rate further, Societe Generale economist Kunal Kundu says. India's GDP growth print of 7.8% for the latest quarter shows "aggregate demand is purportedly absorbing tighter financial and adverse external conditions more comfortably than previously assumed," he says. SocGen revises its previous forecast of two 25bp RBI rate increases to three, bringing the repo rate from 5.25% to 6.00% by early 2027. The change also reflects SocGen's revised expectations of three Fed rate increases between 3Q 2026 and 1Q 2027, compared with no hikes previously. (jihye.lee@wsj.com)
